step1_summary.Chief complaint: Itchy, sore, red skin rash affecting chest, hands, arms for 4 days

Symptoms.severity: severe itching causing sleep disturbance and inability to focus at work
Symptoms.aggravating factors: unclear, no new exposures identified; itching worsens symptoms
Symptoms.alleviating factors: daily showers somewhat ease itching; over-the-counter steroid cream not effective

step1_summary.Vital signs/exam findings: Not explicitly reported; rash described as red, itchy, sore with cracked skin, no pus or bleeding

V: Vascular dermatitis unlikely - no signs of vascular insufficiency or hemorrhage noted
I: Contact dermatitis (inflammatory reaction to irritants/allergens) – Given rapid onset and itchy rash, possible irritant or allergic trigger
Secondary skin infection (e.g., impetigo) – less likely since no pus/discharge, no fever
N: Cutaneous lymphoma (rare) – possible but less likely given acute onset and known eczema history
D: Eczema flare-up (Atopic dermatitis) – Most consistent with history and presentation of itchy, cracked skin in typical distribution
I2: Steroid withdrawal or ineffective OTC treatment – patient used OTC steroid cream without relief, possibly suboptimal potency or incorrect diagnosis
A: Atopic dermatitis (autoimmune/allergic basis) – consistent with previous eczema and itchy rash
T: Skin trauma or irritant exposure – no reported injury but possible unknown irritant
